title: Himeji Castle
blurb: Japan’s White Heron Castle in Himeji, its 46.4 m main keep rising over a cluster of three smaller keeps linked by roofed corridors. This schematic model covers the inner citadel, its maze of gates, stone walls and three moats — a fraction of the full 233-hectare complex.

systems.name: Main keep (Daitenshu)
systems.description: The 46.4 m main keep: five stories outside, six floors plus a basement inside, on its great stone base.

systems.name: Subsidiary keeps (Shōtenshu)
systems.description: The east, west and northwest small keeps that cluster with the main keep.

systems.name: Connecting corridors (Watariyagura)
systems.description: The roofed I, Ro, Ha and Ni passages linking the keeps, with the castle kitchen.

systems.name: Gates (Mon)
systems.description: The maze of gates along the winding approach, from Otemon to the inner maze gates.

systems.name: Stone walls (Ishigaki)
systems.description: Battered stone walls up to 26 m high, with the keep platform, earthen walls and the oil wall.

systems.name: Turret towers (Yagura)
systems.description: Defensive turret towers on the citadel walls.

systems.name: West bailey (Nishi-no-maru)
systems.description: Princess Sen’s west bailey with its hundred-meter corridor and the Kesho Yagura.

systems.name: Moats and water
systems.description: The three concentric moats and the legendary Okiku well.

systems.name: Baileys and courtyards (Kuruwa)
systems.description: The walled baileys and courtyards between the gates.

systems.name: Defensive features
systems.description: Stairs, weapon racks, strong points, stone-drop windows and loopholes.

explanations.main keep stone base (tenshudai): The great stone base carrying the main keep, with battered walls in the musha-gaeshi manner that curve outward to repel climbers. Castle stone walls rise to 26 m at their highest. Exact base height is schematic.
explanations.main keep basement: The keep basement, 385 m2, holding lavatories, a drain board and a kitchen corridor, facilities not seen in other keeps. Exact layout is schematic.
explanations.main keep floor 1 walls: The first floor, 554 m2, called the thousand-mat room for its 330 plus tatami mats, with bugukake racks for matchlocks and spears; the castle once held 280 guns and 90 spears. Exact room divisions are schematic.
explanations.main keep floor 2 walls: The second floor of about 550 m2. From outside, the second and third floors from the top read as a single story, so the keep shows five stories while holding six floors. Exact layout is schematic.
explanations.main keep floor 3 walls: The third floor. The west pillar’s two timbers were joined on this floor during the Showa restoration. Exact layout is schematic.
explanations.main keep floor 4 walls: The fourth floor, shrinking with the keep’s taper. Exact layout is schematic.
explanations.main keep floor 5 walls: The fifth floor. The two great pillars rise from the basement to the fifth-floor beams. Exact layout is schematic.
explanations.main keep floor 6 walls: The sixth and top floor, with panoramic views over Himeji and the Harima Plain. Exact layout is schematic.
explanations.main keep story roof 1: Roof tier over the first story. Himeji’s roofs layer karahafu and chidori hafu gables partly to confuse attackers about the number of levels. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.main keep story roof 2: Roof tier over the second story. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.main keep story roof 3: Roof tier over the third story. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.main keep story roof 4: Roof tier over the fourth story. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.main keep story roof 5: Roof tier over the fifth story. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.main keep great roof: The great top roof of the keep. White roof plaster seals the flat and cylindrical tiles into an impermeable skin that protects the wooden frame from moisture and fire. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.main keep gables (karahafu and chidori h: Curved karahafu gables and triangular chidori hafu plover gables decorating the roof tiers. Exact gable counts are schematic.
explanations.main keep shachihoko ornaments: Golden shachihoko, mythical fish-tigers crowning the great roof ridge, believed to protect the castle from fire. Exact sculpture is schematic.
explanations.main keep ridge-end tiles (onigawara): Oni-gawara demon tiles capping the roof ridge ends; the clan crests of the castle’s lords are stamped into the end tiles of the eaves and ridges. Exact placement is schematic.
explanations.main keep east pillar: The east great pillar, 97 cm across at the base and originally a single fir tree, now mostly replaced. Shown full length so it reads in the exploded view; exact position is schematic.
explanations.main keep west pillar: The west great pillar, 85 by 95 cm at the base, of Japanese cypress. In the Showa restoration a 26.4 m cypress from the Kiso Mountains replaced it; the tree broke in handling, so a second tree from Mount Kasagata was joined to it on the third floor. Shown full length; exact position is schematic.
explanations.main keep top-floor shrine: The small shrine on the top floor of the keep. Exact form is schematic.
explanations.east small keep stone base: Stone base of the Higashi (east) small keep. Exact height is schematic.
explanations.east small keep walls: Wooden walls of the east small keep, one of three subsidiary keeps forming the renritsu-shiki cluster with the main keep. Exact heights are schematic.
explanations.east small keep roofs and shachihoko: Layered roofs of the east small keep with its own shachihoko ornaments. Exact profiles are schematic.
explanations.west small keep stone base: Stone base of the Nishi (west) small keep. Exact height is schematic.
explanations.west small keep walls: Wooden walls of the west small keep. Exact heights are schematic.
explanations.west small keep roofs and shachihoko: Layered roofs of the west small keep with its own shachihoko ornaments. Exact profiles are schematic.

explanations.northwest small keep walls: Wooden walls of the northwest small keep. Exact heights are schematic.
explanations.northwest small keep roofs and shachihok: Layered roofs of the northwest small keep with its own shachihoko ornaments. Exact profiles are schematic.

explanations.ni corridor (ni no watariyagura): The Ni roofed corridor of the keep cluster. Exact route is schematic.
explanations.castle kitchen (daidokoro): The castle kitchen (daidokoro) beside the corridors, part of the National Treasure listing. Exact placement is schematic.
explanations.sakura gate bridge: The Sakuramon-bashi wooden bridge to the Otemon, reconstructed in 2007 to the original Edo-period design. Exact span is schematic.

explanations.ubagaishi millstone: The Ubagaishi: legend says an old woman donated her millstone for the castle walls, and it was set into the stonework here. Shown as a distinct stone; the tale is local legend.
explanations.aburakabe oil wall: The Aburakabe (oil wall), reported as a unique mix of clay, gravel and fermented rice water, extremely hard and practically fireproof. Single-source account; placement is schematic.

explanations.earthen wall roof caps: Tiled caps shedding water from the earthen walls. Exact form is schematic.
explanations.bailey divider walls: Stone walls dividing the baileys so each courtyard could be defended alone. Exact runs are schematic.

explanations.main keep staircases: Steep, narrow staircases between the keep floors, deliberately misaligned to slow attackers. Exact runs are schematic.
explanations.thousand-mat room weapon racks: Bugukake weapon racks of the thousand-mat room, which once held 280 matchlocks and 90 spears. Exact arrangement is schematic.
explanations.corner strong points (musha-damari): Musha-damari: miniature strong points in the four corners of each main floor, where a few warriors could lock themselves and fire loopholes into the keep interior. Exact form is schematic.
explanations.stone-drop windows (ishi-otoshi): Ishi-otoshi stone-drop windows under the keep eaves, for dropping rocks and boiling water or oil on attackers. Exact placement is schematic.
explanations.wall loopholes (sama): Sama loopholes in the citadel walls for matchlocks and bows; 997 firing holes are reported across the castle. Exact spacing is schematic.
explanations.maze approach walls: Low walls shaping the maze-like approach, forcing attackers along exposed zigzag routes. Exact runs are schematic.
